body.statement: Let \(D\) be an effective ordered domain and let a semialgebraic subset of a real closed extension of the fraction field of \(D\) be given by a Boolean formula in finitely many polynomial sign conditions.  There are exact algorithms that compute roadmaps and sample points meeting every semialgebraically connected component, decide realizability after adjoining further polynomial sign conditions, eliminate one block of variables, and encode sampled real algebraic coordinates by real-univariate representations with Thom data.  Their numbers of arithmetic operations, output degrees, and, for integer input, coefficient bit sizes are bounded by explicit computable functions of the number of variables, the number and degrees of the input polynomials, and the input coefficient bit size.

source.locator: Algorithms 13.1, 14.5, and 16.8, and Theorem 16.13; Chapters 11--16, pages 363--634
